name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Tuesday 14 August 1990 (English cryptic)

clue.text: He has magical powers over untreated jam

indicators.note: in an across clue 'over' asks for the word to be turned back to front, read from the other end

blocks.note: untreated, as raw sewage or raw material
to jam is to lock fast, as a stuck mechanism

explanation.surface: A wizard waves his hands over a pot of jam that has not been processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' suggests preserves, fitting the untreated food of the surface, but here it is the verb for sticking fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A warlock is a male witch or sorcerer, someone credited with supernatural powers.

clue.text: Was about right they're blemishes

indicators.note: 'about' means going round, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: taken as written
a standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone was correct about their skin flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: RT is a standard abbreviation for right, as on street signs and in notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Warts are small skin growths, unsightly marks or flaws on the surface.

clue.text: Go back on the opposite side

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to move backwards or undo
second meaning: the back face, as the other side of a coin

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction to cross back over; the two halves are separate senses, one verb and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to retreat or undo, and the noun names the back face of a coin or page.

clue.text: Take lion's share of paintings over

indicators.note: the lion's share is the greater part, so only most of a word is kept and the rest dropped

blocks.note: pictures painted in oil colours

explanation.surface: Someone grabs most of an art collection and hands it over.
explanation.walkthrough: Unresolved: as printed, the wordplay does not give the answer. 'Take lion's share of' suggests a word with letters dropped (perhaps 'spoils', lost in the newspaper's text), and 'over' has no clear job; only the definition is certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paintings are routinely called oils, as in a gallery of oils and watercolours.

clue.text: Don't break off negotiations but risk catching cold

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for staying open to further talks
second meaning, literal: leaving the entrance ajar lets a chill in

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for staying willing to talk is read literally the second time, where an unshut entrance means a draught.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means remaining available for discussion, while its literal sense lets cold air into a room.

clue.text: Rodent giving poor actor disturbed rest

indicators.note: something disturbed has been moved out of its settled order, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: a ham is an overacting, poor performer
the letters of rest, rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad actor's sleep is ruined by a rodent scurrying about.
explanation.definitionFit: The hamster is a small burrowing rodent commonly kept as a pet.

clue.text: Tense Dauphin's gift of tennis-balls to Henry V

definitions.text: Dauphin's gift of tennis-balls to Henry V

blocks.note: first meaning: a grammatical tense, telling past events in the present

blocks.clueFragment: Dauphin's gift of tennis-balls to Henry V
blocks.note: second meaning, playful: a famous gift from history

explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like an adjective for nervous; it is the grammar noun. In Shakespeare's Henry V the French Dauphin mockingly sends the king tennis balls, a gift that really happened in history.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the grammatical device of narrating past events in present tense, and literally a gift recorded by history.

clue.text: Mine agrees change is needed in animal exhibitions

indicators.note: a change is needed, so the order of these letters is altered

blocks.note: both words supply all ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mining company concedes that zoos need reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Menageries are collections of wild animals kept for show, the forerunners of zoos.

clue.text: To doctor, love (the French style) is a lottery

blocks.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O
la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: Choosing whom to marry, French style, is a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a verb but is the qualification MB.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle-style game where tickets are drawn from a revolving drum for prizes.

clue.text: Is inherent in military teams it appears

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
sides are teams, as in a match

explanation.surface: Something is built into the way soldiers organise their squads.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper scan reads 'terms', but the wordplay needs 'teams' for SIDES. RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword stand-in for military.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality that resides in something lives within it, so it is inherent in it.

clue.text: They go round with firearms

blocks.note: first meaning: things that revolve or rotate
second meaning: handguns with a rotating cylinder

explanation.surface: A gang does its rounds carrying guns.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: anything that revolves is a revolver.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols named for their rotating cylinder share the name with anything that turns round and round.

clue.text: Identifies celebrities

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to specify or pin down
second meaning: big ..., famous people

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone spotting famous people; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone is to identify them, and famous people are called big names.

clue.text: Painful spot on Cupid's back

indicators.note: the god's name read backwards, as if seen from behind

blocks.note: Eros is the Greek counterpart of Cupid, the god of love

explanation.surface: Cupid has a tender spot on his back, perhaps from his quiver strap.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupid's back looks like a body part; it means EROS written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore is a tender, painful place on the skin, such as an ulcer or inflamed patch.

clue.text: Keep firm grip?

blocks.note: first meaning: the central tower of a castle
second meaning, playful

explanation.walkthrough: Keep looks like a verb; it is the noun for a castle's main tower. The question mark flags that the second meaning splits the answer into strong + hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle keep is a fortified tower, and a fortress of that kind is a stronghold.

clue.text: Downright about-turn may be more honourable

indicators.note: to turn something about is to face it the other way, so the short word is written backwards

blocks.note: straight as in plain, direct, outright
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A complete U-turn might make someone more principled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About-turn' looks like one military word; split it, and about gives RE while turn flips it.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest and upright, so straighter is more honest and principled.

clue.text: Annoy over number let out

indicators.note: 'over' in an across clue turns the number back to front
letters that are out are put out of place, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: ten is a number
the three letters of let, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated about a number being released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is tempting as the single letter N, but here it is a whole number word.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate them, like the sting of the plant.

clue.text: fashionable ways to make raids

blocks.note: in fashion, as in 'the in thing'
a way is a road or route

explanation.surface: Trendy routes are being used to launch attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile incursions into enemy territory, the same thing as raids.

clue.text: Storm that to sailors brings trouble

blocks.note: taken as written
the Royal Navy, the body of British naval sailors
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A storm at sea spells trouble for those on board.
explanation.walkthrough: RN, the Royal Navy, is the usual crossword shorthand for sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, a particularly destructive kind of storm.

clue.text: Navigator put up to head company plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means writing it from bottom to top

blocks.note: John Cabot, the Italian navigator who sailed to North America for England in 1497
the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An explorer is installed as head of a manufacturing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory, fitting the company surface, but it is a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is the leafy plant grown and cured for smoking.

clue.text: Get the message to convert into money

blocks.note: first meaning: to understand, become aware
second meaning: to sell assets for cash

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a hint to cash in; the two meanings are unrelated senses of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to grasp something mentally and to turn assets into cash.

clue.text: Puts up a case for soft metals

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
lead is a metal; leads in the plural

explanation.surface: Someone argues in favour of soft metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft metals' looks like one idea, lead being a soft metal, but soft is the P from music.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer who pleads for a client argues on their behalf, presenting their side in court.

clue.text: Pronounce "rescue"

blocks.note: first meaning: to utter formally, as a speech or verdict
second meaning: to save or set free

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like an instruction to say a word; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge delivers a verdict, and to deliver someone from danger is to save them.

clue.text: Suffer terrible danger from turbulent assembly

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to bear is to endure or suffer
the letters of danger, rearranged

explanation.surface: A riotous gathering puts everyone at grave risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear-garden, originally a bear-baiting arena, is a noisy, disorderly scene or rowdy meeting.

clue.text: Friends' reverse is a blow

indicators.note: the friends' word is to be read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Falling out with friends is a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like a setback; it simply turns PALS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a smack with the open hand, a kind of blow.

clue.text: Stopped a large proportion with foot-lever

indicators.note: a proportion is only a part, so the answer is a stretch of the clue's own letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and through the next two

explanation.surface: Someone halted a good share of something by operating a lever with the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal is a lever worked by the foot, as on a bicycle or piano.

clue.text: Bring forth we hear from side

indicators.note: we hear says what follows is taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team produces something, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: In an old sense, to teem is to bear offspring or produce abundantly.

clue.text: Eastwood's antecedent rock-fissure

blocks.note: first meaning: the name that comes before Eastwood, the American film actor
second meaning: a geological term for the blocks or cracks of limestone pavement

explanation.walkthrough: Antecedent sounds like an ancestor, but it is the word that goes before: Clint Eastwood's first name. The second meaning is a geology word, in dictionaries as a crevice in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor's first name doubles as a limestone-pavement term for a fissured rock slab or crevice.

clue.text: Public relations deserve to be modified or maintained

indicators.note: a word modified is altered, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
the letters of deserve, rearranged

explanation.surface: A press office's reputation should either be changed or kept as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something preserved has been kept in good condition, the same as maintained.

clue.text: Deliveries manage to exceed allotted time

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Getting through the bowling is enough to make a cricket match run late.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries are balls bowled in cricket, and a bowler's set of six of them is an over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go on beyond the scheduled finishing time.

clue.text: Quality of sound novice gets from old tambourine

blocks.note: timbre is the tone colour of a voice or instrument
L for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A beginner coaxes a fine tone from an antique percussion instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner because British learner drivers display an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbrel is a biblical-era hand drum or tambourine, an archaic word for one.
